English: Rope Corral
A hastily erected enclosure made from rope and wooden stakes, suitable for temporarily containing yaks on the open steppe.
Yak Shelter
Simple lean-tos covered with hides to protect yaks from wind and snow, improving herd survival in harsh climates.
Wattle Pen
A sturdier pen built from woven wattle and daub, providing improved security and supporting larger yak herds.
Stone Paddock
A well-constructed paddock with stone walls, safeguarding the herd and enabling better herd management.
Fenced Yard
An expansive yard bounded by strong timber fencing, supporting a thriving yak population and improved logistics.
Breeders Pavilion
A specialized pavilion for yak breeders, focusing on selective breeding and herd health, greatly boosting yak productivity.
Expanded Pen
A massive, organized pen system with dedicated caretakers and advanced yak management practices, sustaining unprecedented herd sizes.
Village Yak Hall
A grand communal structure at the heart of the yak village, serving as a center for herders, feasts, and yak-related commerce.
Chiefs Pen
A prestigious enclosure reserved for the clan chiefs prized yaks, symbolizing authority and attracting the best herders.
Tibetan Yak Sanctuary
A legendary, fortified sanctuary of yak culture, faith, and power, revered by all nomads and a beacon for travelers and traders alike.
